newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro markets take fright after U.S. selloff.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro markets take fright after U.S. selloff.

text.p: European investors took fright on Wednesday after watching the wild gyrations of U.S. stock and bond markets overnight.

On foreign exchange markets, the dollar started the European session on a bullish note after hitting fresh highs against the yen overnight. It was also strong against the mark. Analysts said it could see a slight correction, particularly against the yen, but there would be no real change to its upward trend.

Two of Europe's major bourses, London and Paris, started the day well down and bonds tracked lower after the late shakeout on Wall Street. Frankfurt's screen-based IBIS DAX index also fell sharply, alhough the 30-share DAX rose in early trading as it sought to catch up with Tuesday's post-bourse rally.
The nerves all stemmed from Wall Street's see-saw performance.

U.S. blue chips rose more than 100 points on mild inflation news before profit-taking wiped out all the gains to send the Dow Jones industrial average to its fifth consecutive loss with a decline of 4.61 points.
Wall Street shadowed the volatile bond market which saw the Treasury's key 30-year security rally more than a full point before losing steam. Bonds gave up most of their gains to end modestly higher.
"It was definitely a shock to see the Dow Jones ending lower after being up 100 points," one German dealer said.
"People are now pretty sceptical again and they're looking out for the durable goods report this afternoon," said another. The key U.S. economic report is due out at 1330 GMT.
British shares slid in early trading, giving back Tuesday's gains after investor nerves were unhinged by Wall Street.
"We've had another predictable mark down. The Dow falls and we have a poor open," the head of trading at large brokerage said.
Dealers said with the FTSE 100 down 31 points at 4,206 by 1015 GMT the market was waiting to see which way Wall Street would jump later.
"I wouldn't look for any large-scale selling this morning," the trader added. "Wall Street is looking vulnerable but until we see a decisive break (lower) we'll just limp along."
French shares shed some of Tuesday's sharp gains in early trading, but traders said they were not too worried about the Paris market.
The bourse needed a pause after recent strong advances, they said, and the continued strength of the dollar provided support.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 23 points or nearly one percent, 2,459 at 1015 GMT.
Conglomerate Bouygues rose 1.7 percent to 537 francs after reporting 1996 net attributable profit of 650 million francs ($116 million).

After early sharp falls in German screen-based trading, the 30-share DAX index opened floor trading up a few points as it sought to catch up with Tuesday's late afternoon rally. Floor trade had closed before U.S. wage cost data was released.
Traders said they expected the market to remain range-bound through the day, although the dollar's strength was providing support.
The dollar edged up in early European trade but remained short of its 31-month high of 1.6570 marks and 47-month peak against the yen of 122.78.

"The economy in the U.S. is looking very good, so the dollar has more of an upside in general...But I think we'll see the yen strengthening a bit today," said Glenn Davies, chief economist at Credit Lyonnais Laing in London.
The apparent willingness of the Japanese authorities to let the dollar rally run its course was one factor exerting quite an influence, analysts said.
Sterling was firm against the mark, rising to a high of 2.6685 before slipping to around 2.6675. The mark was steady to slightly firmer against other European currencies.
CURRENCIES AT 1015 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6523 marks and 122.58 yen compared with late Tuesday's European level of 1.6496 marks and 121.31 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1015 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading shares was down 31.4 points, or 0.74 percent, at 4,206.0.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 23.0 points, or 0.93 percent, at 2,459.76.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 15.45 points, or 0.52 percent, at 3,004.59.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold opened $1.40 lower at $351.65 against $353.05 at the London close on Tuesday. Traders said OTC options expiry Wednesday could lead to a test of $350, then to recent lows around $346. Silver was three cents weaker at $4.95.
